items.q: Which of these is NOT one of the six numbered presentations of glomerular disease on this page?
items.exp: The list is 1. Asymptomatic, 2. macrohematuria, 3. nephrotic syndrome, 4. nephritic syndrome (acute glomerulonephritis), 5. RPGN, 6. chronic kidney disease (chronic glomerulonephritis). (Book p756)

items.q: Hyperlipidemia and lipiduria are noted on this page as having previously formed part of the diagnostic criteria for nephrotic syndrome.
opts: True — the note says they were previously part of the criteria
False — they are the third and fourth printed criteria
False — they were never part of the criteria
True — and they replace the hypoalbuminemia criterion in children
items.exp: Beneath the three printed criteria the note reads: 'Hyperlipidemia, lipiduria were previously part of diagnostic criteria'. (Book p756)

items.q: Fill up: The third criterion of nephrotic syndrome is oedema, which the page describes as ______ oedema.
items.exp: Criterion 3 is written as 'Edema : Extravascular', with 1 Nephrotic range proteinuria and 2 Hypoalbuminemia <3 g/dl. (Book p756)

items.q: A 6-year-old has nephrotic-range proteinuria, serum albumin 3.4 g/dL and periorbital puffiness. Applying the criteria box, this child:
opts: Meets childhood nephrotic syndrome, since children need 1 plus 2 or 3
Does not meet it, because all three criteria are mandatory at any age
Meets it only if hyperlipidemia is also demonstrated
Cannot be classified until a renal biopsy is done
items.exp: The bracket beside the criteria prints 'Adults: 1 + 2 + 3' and 'Children: 1 + 2 or 3', so criterion 1 with edema alone satisfies the paediatric definition. (Book p756)

items.q: In the biopsy-indication flowchart, proteinuria ALONE prompts biopsy once it exceeds:
items.exp: The asymptomatic arm lists two routes: proteinuria >500 mg/24 hrs plus microhematuria ≥3 RBC/HPF, or proteinuria alone >1 g/24 hrs. (Book p756)
